title: grun environment configuration
description: One file per environment. Supplied at synth time with -c config=<path>. Every particular (accounts, hostnames, ARNs, endpoints) lives here, not in this repository.

env.description: Environment name. The stack is called grun-<env> and every IAM role is named grun-<env>-...

account.description: Account id. Optional: defaults to the account of the credentials (CDK_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT).

network.description: An existing VPC. Runner tasks run in its public subnets with a public IP (no NAT).

publicSubnetIds.description: One public subnet per availability zone, in the same order.

securityGroupIds.description: Existing security groups for the runner tasks. Empty or absent: the stack creates one (no inbound rule) and prints its id.

permissionsBoundary.description: Name of the permissions boundary policy applied to every role of the stack.

cdk.description: The CDK bootstrap the stack deploys through.

qualifier.description: The CDK qualifier of the bootstrap: its roles and buckets are named cdk-<qualifier>-*. It must be the qualifier the account was bootstrapped with, and the Qualifier the Deploy boundary was rendered with.

sluis.description: Where the GitHub Apps' credentials come from: a role in the account that holds them, assumed by the secret-sync Lambda.

region.description: Region of the SSM parameters. Default: the stack region.

repository.description: The base image repository, through the account's ECR pull-through cache: <account>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com/<cache prefix>/<path>.

version.description: Tag of the ci-plane runner image. Changing it rebuilds the runner image on the next deploy.

runnerVersion.description: GitHub Actions runner version baked in: 'latest' (resolved at each build) or an exact version.

rebuildIntervalDays.description: Scheduled rebuild (picks up runner releases and OS updates). GitHub rejects runners older than 30 days, keep this well below. 0 disables.

computeType.description: CodeBuild compute type of the image build (Arm).

extraCertificates.description: Private CA trusted by the image. Give a path (relative to this file) or the PEM itself.

shapes.description: Runner sizes. One Fargate ARM provider per shape and organisation; the label is what a job puts in runs-on. Default: fg-large 4 vCPU/12 GB, fg-medium 2/8, fg-small 1/4, fg-xsmall 0.5/1, and fg-medium-spot 2/8 on Fargate Spot, fg-xlarge 8/16.

spot.description: Run the tasks on the FARGATE_SPOT capacity provider. An interruption fails the job it runs; GitHub does not retry it. Never for a stable tier.

requireSelfHostedLabel.description: Require the self-hosted label in runs-on. False lets a job say runs-on: fg-large alone.

runnerEnvironment.description: Environment of the runner tasks: the cache endpoints the shared CI workflows read, and any extra variables.

nixSubstituter.description: The Nix pull-through cache, an http(s) URL without spaces (for example https://nix.example.test/nix). The tasks get NIX_CONFIG with `substituters = <this> https://cache.nixos.org/`, so the upstream stays the fallback.

mavenRegistry.description: CI_RUNNER_MAVEN_REGISTRY: the base of a Maven pull-through cache with one path per upstream (<base>/central, <base>/google, <base>/gradle-plugins), an http(s) URL without spaces (a name of its own with no path of its own, for example https://maven.example.test; ci-plane's cache-redirect serves the repositories under /maven, which the gateway maps from the name's root). The shared setup-devbox step probes it, and Gradle builds then resolve their dependencies and plugins through it.

gradleBuildCache.description: CI_RUNNER_GRADLE_BUILD_CACHE: the URL of Gradle's remote build cache (the HTTP protocol), an http(s) URL without spaces, ending where the key begins (a name of its own with no path of its own, for example https://gradle.example.test; ci-plane's cache-redirect serves it at the root of its build cache front-end). The cache is WRITABLE by the jobs: name the cache of this stack's own environment, so that a tier reads only what its own jobs wrote.

goCacheBucket.description: CI_RUNNER_GOCACHE_S3_BUCKET: the S3 bucket of this runner's Go build cache and archive caches. The shared actions prefer it over the caller's organisation variable, so a tier uses its own bucket whatever the caller passes.

goCacheRegion.description: CI_RUNNER_GOCACHE_S3_REGION: the region of goCacheBucket. Needs goCacheBucket.

buildxCache.description: CI_RUNNER_BUILDX_CACHE: the registry reference of the BuildKit cache (<registry>/<repository>, no tag), preferred by the shared workflows over the caller's organisation variable.

buildkit.description: mTLS towards the shared build farm. The client certificate comes from Secrets Manager and is written to files in one directory before the runner starts.

tlsDir.description: CI_BUILDKIT_TLS_DIR: a plain absolute path. Holds ca.pem, cert.pem and key.pem.

arn.description: Complete ARN of a JSON secret.

costTags.description: Cost allocation tags. The stack carries <componentKey>=<componentValue> and <environmentKey>=<env>; each organisation's resources and runner tasks carry <companyKey>=<organisation name>. The daily budget filters on <componentKey>=<componentValue>. Activate the keys in Billing.

runner.description: Settings of the runner tasks beyond the environment.

secretEnv.description: Environment variables that ECS fills from SSM Parameter Store (SecureString) when a task starts. Maps the variable name to the parameter name or ARN. The task definition holds the parameter reference, never the value; the execution role may read exactly these parameters.

idleTimeoutMinutes.description: Minutes a runner may stay registered and idle (no job taken) before the idle reaper stops it and removes it from GitHub; measured from its registration. A runner started for a job that GitHub then cancelled or gave to another runner disappears after this time instead of waiting to serve a later job. Busy runners and the warm runners (their pool's duration governs them) are not affected. Absent: the library's default of 5.

logRetentionDays.description: Retention of the runner tasks' own log groups (the runner container's stdout and the init container's). Absent: logRetentionDays. The orchestration functions, the state machine and the image builder keep logRetentionDays.

requeue.description: Every five minutes, start a runner again for each job that is still queued in a run of which a runner of this stack ended without a job (the idle reaper) or failed to start, less the runners still running for that run. GitHub sends the queued webhook once, so a matrix job made runnable by max-parallel after its runner was reaped would otherwise stay queued. The task cap holds; jobs queued for more than six hours and finished runs are left alone. Absent or true: on.

traceToStdout.description: Copy the runner's own diagnostic trace (the listener's and the worker's, also written to _diag in the task) to the container's stdout and so to its log group: ACTIONS_RUNNER_PRINT_LOG_TO_STDOUT. The upstream runner image turns it on, which is almost all of what the log groups ingest. Absent or false: off, and stdout keeps the runner's terminal output only.

secretKmsKeyArn.description: ARN of the customer-managed KMS key that encrypts the secretEnv parameters. The execution role gets kms:Decrypt on it. Omit for the AWS-managed SSM key.

telemetry.description: Where grun-agent sends the runner tasks' OpenTelemetry: the runner's warnings and errors as OTLP logs, the job's peaks as OTLP metrics and one log event. It authenticates with an access token traded (RFC 8693) for the task role's web identity token (sts:GetWebIdentityToken, which the task roles are then allowed for stsAudience). Absent: the agent prints the peaks in the job log and sends nothing.

otlpEndpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP base URL; /v1/logs and /v1/metrics are appended.

issuerUrl.description: Base URL of the token issuer; the exchange is a POST to <issuerUrl>/token.

stsAudience.description: Audience asked of STS for the web identity token. Default: issuerUrl.

otlpAudience.description: Audience and exchange client id of the access token. Default: otlp.

sampleSeconds.description: Seconds between two samples of the task's stats. Default: 5.

onExceed.description: skip: no runner is started and the job waits. defer: the webhook fails and GitHub redelivery retries it for 30 minutes.

warm.description: Warm capacity: runners started ahead of demand on a weekly rhythm. EventBridge rules run in UTC, so the window is given in UTC and chosen to cover local business hours in both summer and winter time.

webhook.description: How GitHub reaches the organisations' webhook functions: an API Gateway custom domain per organisation behind Cloudflare, with mTLS (Authenticated Origin Pulls) on the origin.

truststoreBucket.description: S3 bucket holding the Cloudflare origin-pull CA bundle (PEM).

taskRolesCanWrite.description: Let the runner task roles read and write the bucket.

dashboard.description: Create the CloudWatch dashboard and Logs Insights queries per organisation.

name.description: GitHub organisation (runners register at organisation level).

sluisParameter.description: SSM parameter (in the sluis account) holding the org's App as a github/v1 JSON.

certificateArn.description: ACM certificate for domainName, in the stack region.

taskRole.description: Permissions of the runner tasks of this organisation (the ambient-credentials shim).

statements.description: IAM policy statements in JSON form.

environment.description: Extra environment for this organisation's tasks.

warm.description: Apply the top-level warm pools to this organisation.

allow.description: The webhook allow-list: the provider selector starts a runner only for a job of one of these repositories, and refuses every other job of the organisation (no capacity is spent; a metric AllowRefused is logged). Absent: every job of the organisation is considered. When ANY organisation of the file has a list, the selector refuses jobs of a login that is not in the file at all. workflow and ref come from the webhook payload (workflow_job.workflow_name, workflow_job.head_branch) and only narrow an entry: the repository is the hard part.

repository.description: owner/name of a repository of this organisation; compared case-insensitively.

workflows.description: Names of the workflows (the `name:` of the workflow file) whose jobs may start a runner; exact, case-sensitive. Absent: any workflow.

refs.description: Globs the job's head_branch must match (for a tag push it is the tag name): `*` matches any characters including `/`, nothing else is special; case-sensitive. Absent: any ref. A branch can be named like a tag, so this narrows and does not authenticate.

runnerGroup.description: GitHub runner group the runners of this organisation register in. It must exist before the first job (a runner that cannot join its group does not start); its repository access limits which repositories the runners serve. Absent: the organisation's default group.
